A1.justification: Both PDFs contain the same research work, Efficient Quadratic Corrections for Frank-Wolfe Algorithms. All 40 pages, including Appendices A–F, are readable and support comparison of text, equations, figures, and tables.

before.justification: v4 reports original computational experiments in Section 4 and Appendix F, including convergence trajectories, runtimes, tensor-completion results, and quadratic-correction success counts.

after.justification: v5 retains these original computational experiments and their results in Section 4 and Appendix F, including Figures 1–11 and Tables 1–2.

M1.justification: Algorithms 1–11 retain the same CFW/LCFW framework, QC-LP and QC-MNP corrections, and SCG/SOCGS procedures. The Proposition 1 proof correction does not change any algorithm.

E1.justification: Both versions evaluate synthetic sparse regression, entanglement detection including noisy states, Birkhoff projection and intersection scenarios, gisette logistic regression, and nonnegative tensor completion. No dataset or task scenario is added or removed.

E2.justification: Corresponding experiments retain the same comparators, including FW, AFW, PFW, and BPCG, BCG in tensor completion, and AFW for SOCGS inner steps. Citation substitutions do not change the evaluated methods.

E3.justification: Section 4 and Appendix F retain the same sample sizes, correction intervals, line searches, SOCGS inner-step budgets of 50 and 200, and performance-profile stopping thresholds and limits.

E4.justification: Appendix F retains the same active-set and noise analyses, intersecting/disjoint-set experiments, SCG schedule comparison, SOCGS line-search test, and quadratic-correction success-rate analysis.

E5.justification: Seed information and statistical reporting remain unchanged, including the varying seeds in the 37-instance comparison. No repeated-run information, confidence intervals, or significance tests are added or removed.

E6.justification: Figures 1–11 have identical graphics, and Tables 1–2 retain every result entry. For example, Table 2 reports the same entanglement AFW-MNP successful/total correction count of 492/897. Reported qualitative findings also match.

T1.justification: Appendix A, Proposition 1 changes f(x′) ≤ f(x) to f(x′) ≤ f(x̂) when the short-step size exceeds the feasible bound. This revises the sufficient-descent reasoning rather than merely its notation. The proposition, theorem statements, assumptions, and convergence rates remain unchanged.

C1.justification: The abstract, contribution list, and conclusion retain the same claims about the corrective framework, convergence and face identification, quadratic corrections, SCG rates, SOCGS applicability, and computational acceleration.

C2.justification: Interpretations and limitations remain unchanged, including QC-LP infeasibility, correction-frequency tradeoffs, SCG numerical precision, and SOCGS stopping-rule and Hessian-storage issues.

D1.justification: The Liu et al. source used for the entanglement implementation and setup changes from a private manuscript reference in v4 to an identified preprint with a URL in v5. This adds a documented access route; implementation settings, hardware, and budgets remain unchanged.

R1.justification: Several foundational attributions switch from Lacoste-Julien and Jaggi (2015) to the already cited Lacoste-Julien et al. (2013), and the SCG complexity-bound citation switches from Yudin (1983) to Blair (1985). Other updates largely concern publication metadata for matched works; the overall positioning remains stable.

P1.justification: Edits mainly update bibliography entries and in-text citation labels. Proposition 1 also replaces γmax with λa(x), matching Algorithm 3. The section order and nearly all explanatory prose remain unchanged.

P2.justification: Expanded and reordered references reflow pages 12–14, with limited paragraph reflow elsewhere. All 11 figures and both tables retain their displays, captions, and placements.

improvement.justification: The revised comparison with f(x̂), together with the explicit feasible step bound, makes Proposition 1’s intended descent/drop argument more precise. Identifying a preprint for the previously private entanglement-setup source also improves traceability. These are limited gains with unchanged methods and empirical evidence; the other citation substitutions do not themselves establish stronger scientific support.
